title: International Tax Type Setup — Effective Dates shift earlier for a user in a US time zone
requirementSource: NM-4026 — TestRail C107677–C107680: a US user sees, types, picks and saves the Effective Date as entered
stepsToReproduce: Set the browser time zone to America/New_York and open Tax → International Tax Type Setup for office 1606 (/navigator/locations/1606/taxes/international-tax-type-setup) on e2e.
Search Canada as of 01/01/2000 and read Quebec's Effective Date.
Search Mexico as of 12/31/2099, pick GOV type IVA on an empty province and type 01/15/2030 in Effective Date, then leave the field.
Pick the 20th in that row's calendar.
Enter a GOV Reg. Number and Save; inspect the save request.
expectedBehavior: Quebec shows 01/01/2000; the typed date stays 01/15/2030; the picked day shows the 20th; the save sends 2030-01-15T00:00:00.000Z.
actualBehavior: Quebec shows 12/31/1999; the typed date reads 01/14 while typing and 01/13/2030 after leaving; the picked day shows the 19th; the save sends a date a day early.

verificationLog.finding: Failed identically in the full Tax run (9 workers) and an isolated rerun (4 workers, no retries); the TestRail cases already record the shifted values.
